page: Microsoft Azure F8as_v6 is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB (4.0 GB per vCPU). The CPU architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), and AES encryption extensions. This instance does not include local storage disks or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance, ranking in the top 25% with a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2098.0. Multi-threaded metrics fall largely in the middle 50%, with a PassMark CPU score of 20124.64, Geekbench multi-core score of 10884.0, and stress-ng multi-core score of 24619.48. Memory operations show cached bandwidth reaching 1187.02 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read bandwidth drops into the bottom 25% at 38.15 GB/sec.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio paired with dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores offers consistent compute per vCPU without hardware resource contention. However, the lack of local temporary storage requires remote block storage for persistence, which must be factored into system design. The F8as_v6 is suitable for CPU-bound tasks, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, and medium-scale web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure F8as_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 cores operating at 3.7 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers 4.0 GB of RAM per dedicated vCPU alongside 32 MB of L3 cache and instruction support for AVX-512 vector workloads. The server includes no local storage or GPUs, relying entirely on external storage resources. Benchmark tests demonstrate strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2098.0 and stress-ng single-core performance of 3080.99. Multi-threaded processing and cached memory bandwidth maintain steady mid-tier marks, although uncached large-block read operations register lower throughput. Due to its dedicated physical core configuration and balanced compute capabilities, the F8as_v6 is suited for software builds, continuous integration workloads, compression pipelines, and general compute-heavy application hosting.
